title: Flowise Pricing: Plans and Costs (2026 Guide)
summary: Flowise pricing offers a free self-hosted option and cloud plans metered by prediction count and storage.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is Flowise really free?


Is Flowise really free? The software is free, the operation isn't.


Flowise is open source, so you pay no licence fee to run it, but you do pay for the server, the database, the model API calls and the engineer who keeps it patched.


Those costs land on your team instead of on an invoice from Flowise.


### Can I self-host Flowise without paying for a licence?


Yes, for the open source build you can deploy it on your own infrastructure without a licence charge.


What you take on is everything the cloud plans would otherwise cover: upgrades, backups, uptime, access control and security review.


If your organisation needs approval steps before an agent acts, or connectors Flowise doesn't ship, you build and maintain those yourself. Price that labour before you call the deployment free.


### Does Flowise charge per user or per prediction?


On its cloud plans the meter is predictions and storage, not seats. A prediction is a call to a flow, so a chatbot with heavy traffic consumes the allowance faster than a large team that rarely runs anything.


Estimate your monthly run volume first, then compare tiers against that figure. Check the current pricing page for the exact limits, because they change.


Does Flowise offer annual billing or startup discounts? We have no confirmed terms for either, so don't budget around them.


Ask sales directly and get any annual or early-stage discount in writing, along with the prediction and storage limits it applies to. A discount on a tier that your volume outgrows saves you little.


What happens when I exceed my Flowise prediction limit? We haven't confirmed how Flowise enforces the cap, and the behaviour matters.


It may throttle requests, block them or bill overage, and each outcome has a different cost to a live customer-facing agent. Ask for the overage policy in writing before launch, and set usage alerts so you move up a tier before the limit is reached.
